main_body: Tall 16x48 strip of repeating wooden fence posts. The left column holds block-like posts with a tan top and an orange-brown front. The right column is a thin dark-brown post/rail strip with thin grey horizontal rails.
top_band: On the left posts: tan, about rows 0-3, with a diagonal step to the orange front. On the right rails and posts: none, only 1-2 rows of grey at rows ~15, 31 and 47.
evidence: The left posts have a small light cap over a front face, but the cap is a thin, diagonally shaded block with no distinct front-edge line or eave shadow. The right-hand column and the grey horizontal beams are drawn flat and face-on. The beams are only 1-2 rows thick, so they read as rims and not as top surfaces. A frame's beams must show top faces, and these do not. The top is visible only on small parts, so it fails strictly.

style.evidence: The ramps use about 3-4 brown/tan steps. The outlines are dark brown, which fits the material. The post faces and the right column are mostly flat fills with little grain or speckle. The grey rails are one flat tone. Each tile carries only a few colours, far below the stall and well references.
